identity.name: Brahmaputra Infrastructure
identity.industry: Infrastructure EPC / Civil Construction (roads & bridges, railways & tunnels, river/slope protection, institutional buildings) — Northeast-India focused

summary.oneLiner: Niche Northeast-India EPC contractor (river/slope-protection + general civil) at a self-described "inflection point" — FY26 revenue +50% to INR365cr, PAT doubled to INR59.6cr, OB INR1,600cr (4.46x book-to-bill), guiding to sustain ~50% growth for 5 years; embedded high-margin (85%) Guwahati mall annuity differentiates cash flow, but high legacy promoter pledge and govt-payment/working-capital cycle are the watch-items.

one-line thesis: Niche Northeast-India EPC contractor (river/slope-protection + general civil) at a self-described "inflection point" — FY26 revenue +50% to INR365cr, PAT doubled to INR59.6cr, OB INR1,600cr (4.46x book-to-bill), guiding to sustain ~50% growth for 5 years; embedded high-margin (85%) Guwahati mall annuity differentiates cash flow, but high legacy promoter pledge and govt-payment/working-capital cycle are the watch-items.
financial scorecard: Q4 FY26 (standalone): Revenue INR93.93cr · PBT INR16.79cr · PAT INR14.78cr · EPS INR5.09. (Mgmt note: most large orders won in last 4–6 months → revenue recognition lag of 6–7 months, so OB "not yet visible" in Q4.)

Segment FY26: EPC top-line ≈ INR349.81cr (~INR350cr), profit INR51.88cr; Real estate top-line INR19.58cr, profit INR16.70cr (vs INR14.75cr LY). RE revenue dip vs LY = ~INR4cr one-off industrial-plot sales in FY25 not repeated; RE margins improved. EPC ~90% / RE ~10% of revenue (RE ~5–7% per one analyst framing).

Order book: INR1,600 cr as of 31-Mar-26 = 4.46x FY26 revenue (book-to-bill). Split: Buildings INR405cr · Roads & Bridges INR498cr · Railways & Tunnels INR400cr · River Protection INR250cr. ~50% of OB acquired in last 6 months; May-26 orders to be added on top.

Balance sheet / one-offs: Debt declining, D/E improving (no absolute figures given). One-off: FY25 had ~INR4cr industrial-plot sale (RE) not repeated. Working-capital / net-debt figures NOT disclosed on call.
guidance (critical): Revenue growth: Target to maintain ~50% YoY revenue growth for the next ~5 years ("intention and expectation is for the next five years... maintain the same kind of momentum"). Explicitly framed as inflection point, not a one-off.
Profitability: Aim to maintain the same rate of profitability alongside growth.

Order inflow / bid pipeline: Current bid pipeline INR3,000 cr, results expected in 30–45 days; full-year bidding pipeline guided at INR7,000–8,000 cr. Pipeline mix (rough): ~40% buildings, ~20% protection, ~40% roads.
Execution timeline: Of INR1,600cr OB, ~60% executable in FY27, ~40% spills to FY28. Avg project execution 2–3 years (min 2, max 3).

Real estate: New Guwahati open-plaza retail+resi project ~INR500cr over 4–5 yrs, ~4 lakh sq ft leasable; to launch in ~4–5 months; targeting ~INR60cr rental income by ~FY29/FY30; expect RE revenue jump by end of this year post-launch.
order book & pipeline: Current OB: INR1,600 cr (Buildings 405 / Roads & Bridges 498 / Railways & Tunnels 400 / River Protection 250).
Bid pipeline: INR3,000 cr live (decisions in 30–45 days); INR7,000–8,000 cr full-year pipeline.
~70% of OB revenue accrues to BIL, ~30% to JV partners (varies project-to-project).

Growth pipeline themes: NE highway infra, hydropower (Arunachal), border infra/fencing, 5–6 new NE railway lines over 10 yrs (incl. Bhutan/Gelephu line — already bidding), institutional buildings (Assam: university + hospital per district announced).
segment / subsidiary detail: EPC (~90% rev): roads & bridges, railways & tunnels, institutional buildings, river/slope protection, general civil. Clients: NHAI, NHIDCL, MoRTH, NF Railway, Water Resources Departments, state agencies. No HAM exposure — all EPC / item-rate.

Real estate (~10% rev, high margin): City Center Mall Guwahati (operational 7+ yrs, largest mall in NE, 70+ brands first-entry to NE) — stable rental annuity, ~85% margin, minimal incremental capex; Brahmaputra Industrial Park (embedded value). New ~INR500cr plaza project in pipeline.
growth verticals / optionality: River/slope (anti-erosion, geotechnical) protection — flagged as key 5-yr expansion vertical; high-margin niche tied to Brahmaputra flood-prone geography & NE landslide terrain; recurring WRD-department tenders (Assam, Arunachal).
NE structural tailwind: PM Gati Shakti, Bharatmala, Act East, border connectivity, hydropower, NE railway expansion — mgmt positions BIL as a "top beneficiary" with embedded NE execution moat.
Real estate optionality: new plaza mall scaling annuity profit pool.
margins & cost dynamics: Segmental EPC margins range 13%–20%; niche works 18–19%, general infra 11–13%; blended EPC ~15%.
Real estate ~85% margin (almost pure rental yield).

FY26 margin expansion driven by operating leverage + eliminating the historical Q2/Q3 monsoon drag (FY25 had ~nil margins in Q2/Q3) via geographic diversification to lower-monsoon areas — structural, per mgmt.
Margin moat: NE niche + specialized river/slope-protection credentials → fewer qualified bidders → premium vs mainland contractors.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): EPC requires minimal fixed capex; real estate is the capex item: new INR500cr plaza built phase-wise over 4–5 yrs (launch in ~4–5 months — watch for slippage on this "next 4–5 months" launch and on the ~INR60cr-rental-by-FY29/30 target).
Mall annuity needs minimal incremental capex.
capital allocation (debt): Debt has come down meaningfully; D/E improving (no figures given).
Funding new project wins via mix of surety bonds (now accepted across departments) + bank guarantees + JV strategic partnerships rather than heavy balance-sheet leverage.
risks & watch-items: Promoter pledge HIGH — legacy shares pledged since 2014 against earlier higher debt; mgmt "hopes" to get pledge released "in next year or two" as debt falls — not yet done; key overhang.
Revenue-recognition lag (6–7 months) means recent order wins won't show until coming quarters — execution-ramp risk.
Govt-payment cycle / working capital: heavy exposure to govt depts, PSUs, WRD — typical EPC receivable/WC risk (not quantified on call).
Order/geography concentration: heavy Northeast tilt — strength but also single-region dependence; OB diversification across 4 verticals partly mitigates.
~50%-for-5-years guidance is aggressive off a small base; high beat-or-disappoint sensitivity.
JV structure: ~30% of OB revenue flows to partners (BIL captures ~70%).
management quality / tone: First-ever earnings call — confident, growth-oriented, articulate on NE moat; committed to "transparent and consistent" investor engagement going forward.

Candid on softer points (RE revenue dip explained as one-off plot sale; pledge openly addressed). Some numbers not at hand (pipeline break-up). Audio issues during finance presentation. Overall credible but unproven on the public-markets track record; aggressive multi-year guidance to be watched.
non-obvious takeaways: The Q2/Q3 "monsoon drag elimination" is the real driver of the FY26 step-up (Q2+Q3 went INR70cr → INR180cr, 2.6x) — structural geographic-diversification gain, not a demand spike; durability is the key debate.
Mall annuity (~85% margin) gives an EPC name countercyclical cash flow — unusual; underpins claim of "never have cash-flow issues."
~50% of current OB won in last 6 months → reported Q4 understates run-rate; FY27 should show the recognition catch-up if execution holds.
Surety-bond acceptance is a quiet but real capital-efficiency lever for bid capacity without leverage.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers (lis: > No specific competitive challenge/disruption affecting other listed names was discussed. The call was company-specific (NE infra opportunity, own OB/pipeline, pledge). Section intentionally empty.
qoq change log: Q4 FY26 (this): First-ever concall. FY26 rev INR365cr (+50%), EBITDA INR83.45cr (22.83%, +280bps), PAT INR59.61cr (+100%), EPS INR20.54. Q4 rev INR93.93cr / PAT INR14.78cr / EPS INR5.09. OB INR1,600cr (4.46x; Bldg 405 / R&B 498 / Rail&Tunnel 400 / River 250). Bid pipeline INR3,000cr live (30–45 day decisions), INR7,000–8,000cr FY guidance. Guidance: ~50% revenue growth sustained ~5 yrs, maintain profitability; ~60% OB in FY27, ~40% FY28. RE: new ~INR500cr Guwahati plaza (launch ~4–5 months, ~INR60cr rental by ~FY29/30). Risks: high legacy promoter pledge (since 2014), 6–7m rev-recognition lag, NE concentration. No HAM exposure (all EPC/item-rate). No prior call for comparison.

themes.title: Infrastructure EPC & roads order-book conversion
themes.need: India's record capital-outlay cycle (roads, metro, marine, hydro, tunnelling) gives diversified EPC contractors multi-year visibility - AFCONS tracks a ~INR4 lakh cr pipeline (70% domestic) and targets ~INR30,000cr FY27 inflow; NCC/DBL/PNCINFRA/GRINFRA/ASHOKA/CEIGALL carry large road/HAM books; AFCONS/PATELENG/AHLUCONT/PSPPROJECT add marine, hydro and building EPC. The binding issue is execution + client-payment cycles, not order intake.
themes.driver: L1-to-firm-order conversion (AFCONS Croatia/Vadhavan, DMRC awards); NHAI/HAM award pickup; monsoon-end execution ramp.
